relations: Rushing water flow causes the white foam to continuously deform, expand, and contract in the mid-right area.
The stationary rocks and resting twig remain fixed as the turbulent water rushes past them.
The background waterfall feeds the stream, sustaining the continuous churning flow and foam.
caption: The video captures a fixed, low-angle view of a rocky mountain stream, where clear water rushes continuously toward the lower right. In the upper-left background, a small white waterfall spills a steady sheet of falling water onto a sloping rock face. Large grey boulders line both banks, and a mossy foreground rock on the left has a few green leafy sprouts at its base. A thin bare twig rests diagonally across a flat stone in the lower-center foreground, staying anchored in the same pose. The main visible process is the churning flow. A patch of white aerated foam in the mid-right area continuously deforms, expands and contracts, and churns with the current, its shape differing from moment to moment. The turbulence is already active and continues to churn, with no onset or completion visible. The camera remains steady, keeping the rocks, sprouts, and resting twig in place, leaving the moving water as the active element.
